This appeal arises out of the judgment passed in S.C.No.749/2010 dated 05.12.2013 by the XLV Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, wherein the accused were acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 366A, 376 and 109 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short hereinafter referred to as 'IPC'.).

sentences.text: 2. In brief the case of the prosecution is that on 29.12.2009 at about 01:15 p.m., the complainant has taken her minor daughter/the prosecutrix to the computer center for training, situated at Cubbonpet Main Road and she was waiting for her daughter in the second floor.

At 02:00 p.m., the accused Nos.1 to 4 came there and with the help of PW.7 - Kum. Reshma and PW.8 - Kum.Supriya made the prosecutrix to wore a Burkha, to hide her face to avoid identifying the victim from her mother and kidnapped her and took her to Ballavara village, Tarikere taluk, Chikamagalur district and kept in the house of PW.6 - Gowramma.
Knowing fully well that the prosecutrix is a minor girl, the accused induced her and committed the sexual intercourse on her against her will in the house of PW.6 - Gowramma.
The other accused instigated and abetted accused No.1 to kidnap a minor girl.

Aggrieved by the said judgment of acquittal, the State has filed this appeal.

The learned HCGP argued that the learned Sessions Judge has not properly appreciated the evidence on record and the judgment is illegal, erroneous and needs to be set aside.
The reasons assigned by the learned Sessions Judge for acquitting the accused are not proper.
The learned Sessions Judge has failed to appreciate the evidence adduced on behalf of the prosecution in right perspective.
The learned Sessions Judge has failed to drawn the inference from the evidence of prosecution witnesses.
The mother of the victim, PW.1 has supported the case of the prosecution.
Further PW.2 who is the victim has narrated about the kidnap and sexual assault on her.

11.

The learned HCGP argued that the Trial Court without properly appreciating the evidence on record acquitted the accused and hence, the said judgment is illegal, perverse and needs interference by this Court.
With these arguments, learned HCGP prayed to allow the appeal and convict the accused.
7. Against this learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1, 3 and 4 argued that the prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix was a minor girl as on the date of the alleged incident.
The birth certificate - Ex.P22 neither shows the name of prosecutrix nor place of birth or the address of her parents.
Therefore, Ex.P22 will not help the prosecution to prove that the prosecutrix was a minor as on the date of the incident.
Further the case of the prosecution is that PWs.7 and 8 are the friends of victim and with their help, the accused have kidnapped the prosecutrix.
If the age of PWs.7 and 8 are considered, if they are the classmates of prosecutrix, then it is evident that the prosecutrix was not a minor as on the date of the incident.
PW.14/doctor has admitted that the prosecutrix was not subjected to radiological test or dental test so as to ascertain the age of the prosecutrix.

Therefore,
the contention that the kidnapping the minor does not arise.

So this evidence of prosecutrix shows that she is trying to falsely implicate the accused in this case.
9. Learned counsel for the respondents argued that the sister of the prosecutrix was also in love with one Vijay and that Vijay and accused No.1 are friends.
The parents of the victim/PW.2 assuming that accused No.1 would support and help his friend Vijay, filed the false complaint against accused No.1.
Learned counsel also argued that most of the witnesses i.e., panch witnesses - PWs.10 and 11 and PWs.7 and 8 who are the close friends of victim have not supported the prosecution case.

Learned counsel argued that the learned Sessions Judge by taking into consideration all these evidence and materials on record,
has rightly appreciated the evidence in proper perspective and as the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt, had rightly given benefit of doubt to the accused and acquitted the accused.

sentences.text: 21. The other witness - PW.10/Nagesh who is the panch witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.
The rest of the prosecution witnesses are police witnesses and the police officials who have stated about the investigation done by them.

22. On perusing the evidence of official witnesses, it creates doubt about the investigation done by the investigation officer in this case, as none of the witnesses have supported the prosecution case and the medical evidence does not supports the case of the prosecution.

Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly appreciated the evidence of the witnesses and has come to the conclusion that kidnap of the victim by the accused cannot be believed at all and the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused.
There is no material about earlier kidnapping and there is no case registered in that regard.

Even the theory of kidnap stated by the - 20 - prosecutrix that the accused made her to wear Burkha and taken her to Bilekallahalli village and committed sexual assault is doubtful, as none of the witnesses have stated about the same.
The name of the accused is not mentioned in the FIR.
The important witnesses, i.e., PWs.7 and 8 who are the friends of the prosecutrix have not supported the prosecution.

23. As per Exs.P13 and P14, the medical certificate, age of the victim is shown as 15 years, but the age is mentioned not on the basis of any medical test conducted by the doctor, but the age is mentioned in the certificate as stated by PWs.1 and 2.

Ex.P22/birth certificate cannot be considered as a genuine document as in the said certificate, there is no mention of address or place of birth of the victim and it is a suspicious document and relying on the same, the prosecution cannot prove its case.
The medical report and forensic science laboratory report does not support the case of the prosecution.

Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly came to the conclusion - 21 - that the prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix/PW.2-Victim was minor as on the date of the incident and the prosecution has failed to prove its case that the accused has kidnapped the minor girl on the instigation and abetment by the other accused.
Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has come to the conclusion that prosecution has rightly acquitted the accused.

24. Therefore, in view of the discussions stated above and on considering the entire evidence of prosecution witnesses and the judgment of Trial Court, in my considered view the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly given benefit of doubt to the accused.
It is settled principle of law that if two views are possible from the evidence of prosecution witnesses, the view favourable to the accused will have to be accepted.

This Court being appellate Court cannot interfere in the judgment of acquittal by the trial court unless the judgment of acquittal is illegal, perverse,

State of Maharashtra [(2019) 4 SCC 739], while dealing with the power of the appellate court in interfering with the judgment of acquittal held that unless the judgment of trial court is perverse, illegal and not based on sound principles regarding appreciation of evidence, the appellate court shall not interfere in the judgment of acquittal.

sentences.text: Because the judgment of acquittal gives double presumption of innocence to the accused.

26. In view of the principles stated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decisions referred above and on re- assessing the entire evidence of prosecution witnesses, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

The learned Sessions judge has - 23 - considered the entire evidence meticulously and has come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and acquitted the accused by giving benefit of doubt.
I find that the judgment of acquittal passed by the trial court is neither illegal, perverse, erroneous nor the judgment has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
Absolutely, there are no grounds to interfere in the judgment of acquittal.
The appeal being devoid of merit is liable to be dismissed.

27. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The appeal filed by the State-appellant under section 378(1) and (3) Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.

2. Consequently, the judgment and order of acquittal dated 05.12.2013 passed in C.C.No.749/2010 by learned XLV Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH- 46) against the respondents/accused is hereby confirmed.

Ex.P22/birth certificate cannot be considered as a genuine document as in the said certificate, there is no mention of address or place of birth of the victim and it is a suspicious document and relying on the same, the prosecution cannot prove its case.
The medical report and forensic science laboratory report does not support the case of the prosecution.
Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly came to the conclusion - 21 - that the prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix/PW.2-Victim was minor as on the date of the incident and the prosecution has failed to prove its case that the accused has kidnapped the minor girl on the instigation and abetment by the other accused.
Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has come to the conclusion that prosecution has rightly acquitted the accused.
Therefore, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly given benefit of doubt to the accused.
It is settled principle of law that if two views are possible from the evidence of prosecution witnesses, the view favourable to the accused will have to be accepted.
This Court being appellate Court cannot interfere in the judgment of acquittal by the trial court unless the judgment of acquittal is illegal, perverse,
The State Of Karnataka vs J S Chethan on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73819352/
8 - 22 - erroneous and the judgment should have resulted in miscarriage of justice.
25. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sampat Babso Kale and Another v. State of Maharashtra [(2019) 4 SCC 739], while dealing with the power of the appellate court in interfering with the judgment of acquittal held that unless the judgment of trial court is perverse, illegal and not based on sound principles regarding appreciation of evidence, the appellate court shall not interfere in the judgment of acquittal.
Because the judgment of acquittal gives double presumption of innocence to the accused.
26. In view of the principles stated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decisions referred above and on re- assessing the entire evidence of prosecution witnesses, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
The learned Sessions judge has - 23 - considered the entire evidence meticulously and has come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and acquitted the accused by giving benefit of doubt.
I find that the judgment of acquittal passed by the trial court is neither illegal, perverse, erroneous nor the judgment has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
Absolutely, there are no grounds to interfere in the judgment of acquittal.
